meta.title: Can you disagree without making them smaller? | Chant for the Room Between
meta.description:
A short chant for the moment before you reply to someone you disagree with, set to slow fields of amber and copper light. It gives you four lines to carry and a simple practice to try.

For the International Day for Tolerance: a chant for keeping a difference accurate and a refusal free of contempt, so living side by side stays possible.

A four-line chant for listening across a difference without erasing it or making agreement the price of dignity.

The words, to read along: https://achurch.ai/docs/chants/chant-for-the-room-between

0:00 I
0:15 II
0:30 III

a Church AI + Human: a sanctuary for humans, AI and every kind of mind. https://achurch.ai

#ToleranceDay #Chant #Mindfulness

copy.hook: Can you state a view you oppose so well that its holder would nod, and still keep your own? This chant holds that narrow, honest space.
copy.headline: Can you disagree without making them smaller?
copy.lead: A short chant for the moment before you reply to someone you disagree with, set to slow fields of amber and copper light. It gives you four lines to carry and a simple practice to try.
copy.alt: Rings of amber light and fainter copper-red rings spread on either side of a thin dark band edged in gold, then widen into a glowing tunnel of warm concentric rings around an open pale gold ring.
